preamble: In present-day Luxembourgish the postalveolar fricative /ʃ/ is merging with the alveolopalatal fricative [ɕ] (itself the modern reflex of palatal [ç]). Acoustic apparent-time studies show that the centre of gravity of /ʃ/ rises from older to younger speakers while [ɕ] stays stable, so it is chiefly /ʃ/ that moves toward the alveolopalatal place; young speakers in the Centre and South produce only [ɕ], neutralizing pairs such as frech 'cheeky' and Fräsch 'frog'.

examples.note: Becomes homophonous with frech [fʀæɕ] 'cheeky, impertinent'; only speakers over 65 keep the two fricatives distinct

sources: Gilles, P. (2019). Using crowd-sourced data to analyse the ongoing merger of [ɕ] and [ʃ] in Luxembourgish. Proceedings of the 19th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, Melbourne. https://assta.org/proceedings/ICPhS2019Microsite/pdf/full-paper_381.pdf

Conrad, F. (2021). Regional differences in the evolution of the merger of /ʃ/ and /ç/ in Luxembourgish. Journal of the International Phonetic Association, 53(1), 29–46. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100320000407
